title: ScheduleRun
description: One occurrence of something scheduled (RFC-0008): a release's execution or an automation's run. Its id is derived from the subject and `occurrenceAt`, so a second scheduler tick that reaches the same occurrence finds the same row and the effect happens at most once. `state` says whether the run itself completed; `outcome` says whether it did any work, because a run that ended cleanly may still have done nothing. Runs live in D1 and are kept 90 days; the audit log keeps what each call did.

outcome.description: What the run achieved, separately from whether it completed: `did-work` changed something or produced findings; `nothing-to-do`; `proposed` left drafts or proposals for people; `waiting-approval` filed requests a person must decide.

trigger.description: What woke the scheduler: the every-minute cron trigger, the Durable Object clock's alarm, an admin request (backstop), the Node timer, or a person ("Run now", "Publish now").

adjusted.description: The occurrence was moved: `dst-gap` (the wall-clock time did not exist that day, so it ran at the next valid minute) or `tzdata` (the zone's rules changed after it was planned).

summary.description: The agent's own account of the run (`end_run`) or the built-in job's report line. Plain text written by an agent: Studio renders it as text and never as an instruction.

ScheduleRunId.description: A run id: `run_` and 6 to 32 letters or digits, derived from the subject id and `occurrenceAt` (the occurrence's idempotency key).

ScheduleRunState.description: `due`: claimed occurrence not started yet; `ready`: an agent task's window is open and waits for `begin_run`; `running`; `succeeded`; `failed`; `missed`: the window closed or the scheduler came too late; `skipped`: a missed occurrence coalesced into a later one; `budget-exceeded`; `killed`: stopped by a pause or a kill switch.

ScheduleRunWindow.description: An agent task's run window: the automation's key is valid only between `opensAt` and `closesAt`, and only inside a run it began.

ScheduleRunUsage.description: What the run used against its budget, counted by the server.

ScheduleRunTaint.description: The run read visitor-supplied text at `at` through `tool`; from then on it may only read, label, hide and pause.
